state: Can is a draft business language; its compiler/runtime are not implemented. We are designing recovery for a physical-mail notice, not payment or physical forwarding. Existing requirements require staff authority, current verified recipient checks, visible uncertain/failed delivery and stable retry identities. The email capability only sends a typed request; it has no application-callable reconcile operation. The runtime freezes destination/content and can retry the SAME delivery identity under its existing bounded policy. A new source send creates a NEW delivery. Receipts expose identity/status/result/error, not the request. Unknown may already have sent. Failed may represent an invalid typed reply after the email was sent; error text/code proves neither nonacceptance nor retry permission. Skipped means an undispatched ineligible/superseded intent. Successful acceptance is not reading or collection. The current app retains only its latest receipt association; successful matching callbacks change received to notified, never custody. Collection/forwarding/return make new collection notices ineligible. Service expiry alone must not prevent resolution of held property. Proposed common safeguards for any new notice: retain its request and old receipt as immutable staff-only business evidence; freeze account, address, subject and body; require current location staff, exact current recipient/account/address, uncollected state and latest-attempt correlation; recheck these at dispatch; record staff reason/attribution; keep automatic reminder counts unchanged; reject pending or succeeded attempts as failure recovery. Replaying a user request never sends twice. Current authoritative succeeded receipt can repair a missed received-to-notified callback without provider contact. No option can invent an email status-query API or prove external nonacceptance from free text. Compare these choices for application recovery beyond existing automatic retries; they differ in policy/cost, not in the shared safeguards. No production/provider execution is authorized.

recovery_policy.instructions: Which bounded recovery policy should the next complete Can/desired-JavaScript witness adopt? Balance useful staff recovery, preserving uncertainty, source simplicity, duplicate-email risk and the absence of a provider reconciliation operation. This is advisory design selection, not a correctness guarantee.

criteria.runtime_only: Expose old receipt outcomes and repair a known-success callback, but allow no new email from failed/unknown/skipped notice recovery. Existing runtime identity-preserving retries remain the only retry route. This minimizes authored state and duplicate decisions, but exhausted/unresolved deliveries cannot be recovered through a staff business action until shared runtime/provider tooling exists.
criteria.evidenced_resend: Allow a fresh frozen-request send only after staff records a provider-check attestation of nonacceptance; skipped undispatched notices need only a reason. Keep the original receipt unchanged and recheck it. This demands a stronger recorded review before another email, but adds manual outside-provider work and cannot turn an assertion into authoritative transport proof; some outages remain blocked.
criteria.acknowledged_resend: Allow current location staff to request an additional frozen notice after failed/unknown with a nonempty reason and explicit possible-duplicate acceptance, or after skipped with a reason. Give it a new identity and retain the old ambiguous receipt unchanged. This provides an actionable bounded recovery using existing effects and makes the tradeoff explicit, but consciously permits a duplicate email and adds a frozen notice history. It never claims to retry or reconcile the original transport intent.
